findings.detail: The negative cost is the prior-period commitment fair value loaded into a field absent from the commitments schedule; current fair value is separately and correctly extracted.

rationale: This is a Class 2 within-row localization issue. The raw commitments schedules do not disclose amortized cost. For AI Titan, the extracted cost of -34,000 matches the prior-period fair value of (34) at table 46 row 38, while the current-period fair value is (103) at table 25 row 6 and is separately stored as -103,000. AlphaSense independently repeats the pattern: stored cost -10,000 matches prior fair value (10), while current fair value is (30). Thus the negative cost flags identify a comparative-period fair-value-to-cost mapping defect, not legitimate source-reported costs.
